chapter_title: Concerning the Three Blows that befell the Enemy because of the Light.
chapter_note: Despite a brief dialogue/frame seam in ¶1, the chapter is dominated by impersonal, systematic eschatological-cosmological exposition: a numbered threefold structure detailing successive defeats/bindings of the Enemy by Light powers. No NT citation or institutional/pastoral extension appears in the transmitted paragraphs; the reported chapter-level fatigue signal is not borne out in this excerpt.

paragraphs.core_text: The Darkness itself, the Enemy, has received three bad blows with three wars; and worse dangers from the Light in those three wars.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed opening dialogue/frame attribution (“Once again he turned, and says:”) as a later hagiographic wrapper around the teaching.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening formula (“Once again… says:”) signals compilation frame; the remaining sentence is a schematic, impersonal, numbered teaching incipit typical of the core layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The first: (The enemy) was brought out to the middle and separated from his dark earth, whence he had departed. He was vanquished in that first war, caught and [bound] by the living soul.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered sequence (“The first”), cosmological geography (“middle”, “dark earth”), and named salvific power (“living soul”) in expository voice indicate core cosmological teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: The second blow is the time when he will be dissolved and melted, and he perishes in this great fire. He is destroyed and overthrown, from the images that are all by which he exists. And he will be gathered in [to the] fetter corresponding to his archetype, and be made like he was from the first beginning.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic eschatological mechanics (dissolution, melting, fire, reconstitution “like… from the first beginning”) and technical correspondential language (“archetype”) in impersonal exposition mark an old teaching stratum.

paragraphs.core_text: The third blow that will befall the Enemy is the 'rolling back' [at the] end when everything will be separated, and male will be divided [from] female. Now, the male will be bound in the lump, but the female [will be thrown] in to the tomb. For it will be divided [ ... by a great] stone in their midst, for generation upon generation, for ever and ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the numbered triad with eschatological separation and binding imagery (lump/tomb; great stone). No ecclesial instruction or citation; this reads as core mythic-cosmological exposition (even if rhetorically heightened).

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.106⟩ This is the way that the binding of the enemy will come about, in a fetter that is burdensome and strong, one from which there is never escape; because [they have achieved] his binding and bound him for ever. And they have achieved his being set apart, and he has been set apart for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative, process-focused closure of the cosmological sequence (binding/set-apart forever) without hagiographic rejoicing, church discipline, or NT appeal; retains core eschatological mechanism language.
